message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies. Some of the most well‑known signers include:

| Signer | Colony / State | Notable Contributions |
|--------|----------------|------------------------|
| **John Hancock** | Massachusetts | His large, bold signature became a symbol of the act; he later served as President of the Continental Congress. |
| **Thomas Jefferson** | Virginia | Principal author of the Declaration; later became the third U.S. President. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** | Pennsylvania | Renowned statesman, scientist, and diplomat; helped secure French support during the Revolution. |
| **George Washington** | Virginia | Commander-in-chief of the Continental Army; later became the first U.S. President. |
| **James Madison** | Virginia | “Father of the Constitution”; later became the fourth U.S. President. |
| **Samuel Adams** | Massachusetts | Key organizer of the Boston Tea Party; influential political thinker. |
| **John Adams** | Massachusetts | Later became the second U.S. President; key advocate for independence. |
| **Patrick Henry** | Virginia | Famous for his “Give me liberty, or give me death!” speech. |
| **John Jay** | New York | Later became the first Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. |
| **Alexander Hamilton** | New York | Later became the first Secretary of the Treasury. |
| **Robert Livingston** | New York | Later became the first Governor of New York. |
| **John Witherspoon** | New Jersey | Later became the first President of Princeton University. |
| **George Wythe** | Virginia | Influential legal scholar; taught Thomas Jefferson. |
| **John Dickinson** | Pennsylvania | Known as the “Penman of the Revolution”; later opposed the Constitution. |
| **George Clinton** | New York | Later became the first Vice President under George Washington. |
| **William Floyd** | New York | One of the few signers from New York. |
